title: Small generators for the saturated trivial cofibrations
statement: Fix a universe and let $\mathcal A$ be a category with small Hom sets and all small limits and colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable: for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$ it is generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ whose functors $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserve those colimits. A cardinal $\kappa$ is regular if a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ has size less than $\kappa$; a category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone. Let $C,W$ be classes of arrows of $\mathcal A$, and let $\mathcal A^{[1]}$ be its category of arrows and commuting squares. Use arrow retracts as defined in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Call an arrow class weakly saturated if it contains all isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and arrow retracts; a transfinite composition is the map from the first object to the colimit of an ordinal-indexed sequence continuous at limit ordinals. Assume $C$ is weakly saturated and generated as such by a small subset $C_0$, that $C\cap W$ is weakly saturated, and that $W$ has two-out-of-three: for composable $f,g$, membership of any two of $f,g,gf$ in $W$ implies membership of the third. Assume also that the full subcategory on $W$ is accessible: for some infinite regular $\lambda$ it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits in the arrow category and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Then there is a small subset $S\subseteq C\cap W$ which generates $C\cap W$ as a weakly saturated class.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, printed pp. 821–823 (PDF pp. 839–841, numbered from 1), hypotheses (1)–(4) and conclusion. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag for this model-category recognition input.

proof.text: Every isomorphism belongs to $C\cap W$ by the assumed weak saturation of that intersection, hence belongs to $W$. In particular both component isomorphisms of an isomorphism in the arrow category, and their inverses, belong to $W$.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, hypotheses (1)-(4), printed pp. 821-823; elementary repleteness verification for applying the existing replete formulation.

proof.text: The full subcategory on $W$ is replete. Indeed, let $f:X\to Y$ lie in $W$ and let $(a,b):f\to g$ be an isomorphism in the arrow category, with $a:X\to X'$, $b:Y\to Y'$. Its inverse commuting square shows that $a,b$ are isomorphisms in $\mathcal A$, and its commuting equation gives $ga=bf$, hence $g=bfa^{-1}$. By step 1, $a^{-1},b\in W$. Applying two-out-of-three to the pairs $(a^{-1},f)$ and $(fa^{-1},b)$ gives $fa^{-1}\in W$ and then $g\in W$. This proves closure under every isomorphism of arrows, without adding a repleteness hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, hypotheses (1)-(4), printed pp. 821-823; elementary repleteness verification for applying the existing replete formulation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-intersection-generators] in the fixed universe to the same $\mathcal A,C,W$. Its locally presentable and cocomplete ambient category is exactly the one assumed here (the additional completeness of this item is not needed). Its hypothesis (i) holds for the given small generating subset $C_0$; (ii) is the assumed weak saturation of $C\cap W$; the filtered-colimit closure and small generating family in (iii) are the stated accessibility assumption, with the same infinite regular $\lambda$, and its repleteness requirement is step 2; (iv) is the given two-out-of-three property. The cited conclusion supplies a small $J\subseteq C\cap W$ whose weakly saturated closure is $C\cap W$. Set $S=J$, which is precisely the required conclusion.
